statements.C2: Implements ADR 0002 (all active rules in compiled instructions) and ADR 0003 (static hook dispatchers).
statements.NFR1: **Idempotency & Determinism (E1):** Output ordering (levels, rules, JSON keys) MUST be deterministic so consecutive `compile` runs produce zero diff across OSes.
statements.NFR2: **Zero External Packaging Dependencies:** Skills are embedded via `go:embed` (`skills/embed.go`) with zero Node/npm runtime requirement.
statements.NFR3: **Exit Code Semantics (D-73):** `0` = compiled cleanly, `1` = blocking conflicts prevented compilation, `2` = configuration/lock/I/O error.
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN `internal/compile` updates a shared Markdown file (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`), the system SHALL insert or replace content strictly between `<!-- gradus:begin view_hash=... -->` and `<!-- gradus:end -->` markers while preserving all surrounding human-written content.
statements.R1.AC2: WHEN `agents-md` is configured in `targets`, the system SHALL render all active project-wide rules (excluding `user`-level rules) in pyramid order with rule ID, severity, provenance, text, and rejected rationalizations inside `AGENTS.md` (ADR 0002).
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN `claude-code` is configured in `targets`, the system SHALL generate a `CLAUDE.md` managed section, scoped `.claude/rules/gradus-*.md` files with `paths` frontmatter for non-global rules, and `CLAUDE.local.md` for `user`-level rules.
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN `claude-code` is configured in `targets`, the system SHALL generate or merge `.claude/settings.json` with static `PreToolUse` (`gradusctl guard`) and `SessionStart` (`gradusctl status --brief`) hook dispatchers (ADR 0003) plus `permissions.deny`/`permissions.ask` entries for project `permission` rules without removing unrelated user settings.
statements.R2.AC3: WHEN `claude-code` is configured in `targets`, the system SHALL extract embedded Gradus skills from `skills/embed.go` into `.claude/skills/gradus-*/SKILL.md`.
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN `antigravity` is configured in `targets`, the system SHALL generate an `AGENTS.md` managed section, project rule files under `.agents/rules/gradus-*.md`, and user-level rule files under `.agents/rules/gradus-user-*.md` with trigger frontmatter (`trigger: always_on` for global `**/*` rules, `trigger: glob` with `globs` for scoped rules).
statements.R3.AC2: The system SHALL split generated `.agents/rules/gradus-*.md` files whenever appending the next rule would exceed `11,500` characters, ensuring every generated file stays strictly below `12,000` characters (E1).
statements.R3.AC3: WHEN `antigravity` is configured in `targets`, the system SHALL generate or merge `.agents/hooks.json` with static `PreToolUse` (`gradusctl guard`) and `SessionStart` (`gradusctl status --brief`) dispatchers (ADR 0003) and extract embedded Gradus skills into `.agents/skills/gradus-*/SKILL.md`.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl compile` runs on a conflict-free pyramid, the system SHALL write all target outputs deterministically such that a second consecutive run produces zero byte differences on disk (E1), and exit with code `0`.
statements.R4.AC2: IF the resolved pyramid contains one or more blocking conflicts, THEN `gradusctl compile` SHALL leave existing target files untouched and exit with code `1`.
statements.R4.AC3: IF configuration, lockfile verification, or source resolution fails, THEN `gradusctl compile` SHALL report the error to stderr and exit with code `2`.

statements.C2: Must build statically with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and invoke `git` only via `os/exec` if needed.
statements.NFR1: **Secret & PII Redaction (T4, P16):** Lesson persistence MUST redact secrets and email addresses before disk write and MUST omit personal user-activity metrics.
statements.NFR2: **Deterministic Project Key & Cross-Platform Paths:** Project keys for `~/.gradus/lessons/<project-key>/` and finding paths MUST normalize slashes and paths identically across macOS, Linux, and Windows.
statements.NFR3: **Exit Code Contract (D-73):** Technical errors (invalid YAML/JSON, missing rule IDs, locked target level on `--move`, missing `gradus.yaml`) MUST exit with code `2`.
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl conflicts --candidates` runs, the system SHALL compare active rules across distinct levels or overlays whose `scope` patterns overlap and that share tags or significant statement keywords, skipping pairs already recorded in `.gradus/findings/` with identical `hash_a` and `hash_b`.
statements.R1.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl conflicts --confirm --rule-a <id> --rule-b <id>` runs, the system SHALL write or update a finding record in `.gradus/findings/` with `status: confirmed` and current rule content hashes so subsequent `resolve` and `verify` runs treat it as a blocking semantic conflict.
statements.R1.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl conflicts --dismiss --rule-a <id> --rule-b <id>` runs, the system SHALL write or update a finding record in `.gradus/findings/` with `status: dismissed` and current `hash_a` and `hash_b` so the unchanged pair is not surfaced again by `--candidates`, while surfacing again if either rule's content hash changes.
statements.R1.AC4: WHEN `gradusctl conflicts` runs without mutation flags, the system SHALL list existing `.gradus/findings/*.yaml` records and exit with code `0`.
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl lessons add` runs with `--kind`, `--statement`, and optional `--level`, `--enforcement`, or `--evidence`, the system SHALL persist a lesson JSON file conforming to `spec/v1/schema/lesson.schema.json` under `~/.gradus/lessons/<project-key>/` (or `--lessons-dir` override) with zero personal activity metrics (P16).
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN persisting or updating a lesson, the system SHALL automatically redact common secrets and PII (such as API tokens `ghp_...`, `sk-...`, `AKIA...`, Bearer tokens, and email addresses) from `statement` and `evidence` with `[REDACTED]` before writing to disk (Threat Model T4).
statements.R2.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl lessons list` or `gradusctl lessons update --id <id>` runs, the system SHALL list stored lessons or update a lesson's `status` (`open`, `proposed`, `promoted`, `dismissed`) and/or increment `occurrences`.
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl reconcile` runs without `--restore` or `--move`, the system SHALL inspect compiled target outputs against `PlanCompile` and list every drifted file, exiting with code `0` when clean and code `1` when drift exists.
statements.R3.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl reconcile --restore` runs on a workspace with compiled-target drift, the system SHALL re-apply `compile.ApplyCompile` deterministically to restore generated sections and files, returning exit code `0`.
statements.R3.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl reconcile --move --rule-file <path> --target-level <id>` runs targeting an unlocked level (`locked: false`), the system SHALL move or copy the rule file into that level's `rules/` directory and exit with code `0`.
statements.R3.AC4: IF `gradusctl reconcile --move` targets a `locked: true` or unknown level, THEN the system SHALL refuse the modification without altering the target level and exit with code `2`.

statements.C1: Uses `github.com/spf13/cobra` for CLI routing and `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` for YAML/frontmatter parsing.
statements.C2: Implements ADR 0004 (strict level derivation from container location) and `docs/design/gradus-design.md` §9.1–§9.5.
statements.NFR1: **Zero CGO & Cross-Platform Paths:** All schema parsing, `init`, and `explain` operations MUST compile with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and handle both POSIX (`/`) and Windows (`\`) filesystem paths cleanly.
statements.NFR2: **Canonical English:** All generated files, error messages, CLI help text, and specifications MUST be written in English.
statements.NFR3: **Exit Code Determinism (D-73):** Configuration, schema, and lookup errors MUST strictly return exit code `2`, never `0`.
statements.R1.AC1: The system SHALL provide `spec/v1/SPEC.md` documenting the `gradus/v1` schema for `gradus.yaml`, `level.yaml`, `overlay.yaml`, rule Markdown frontmatter, `gradus.lock`, resolved views, evidence records, lessons, and exceptions.
statements.R1.AC2: The system SHALL provide valid JSON Schema files under `spec/v1/schema/` for `gradus`, `level`, `overlay`, `rule-frontmatter`, `lock`, `resolved-view`, `evidence`, `lesson`, and `exception`.
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN `internal/schema` parses a valid `gradus.yaml` (`schema: gradus/v1`, non-empty ordered `levels` with unique IDs matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`), the system SHALL return the typed pyramid configuration with zero errors.
statements.R2.AC2: IF `gradus.yaml`, `level.yaml`, or `overlay.yaml` contains malformed YAML, an unsupported `schema` value, duplicate level IDs, or a level ID failing `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, THEN the system SHALL return a descriptive validation error that maps to CLI exit code `2`.
statements.R2.AC3: WHEN `gradus.yaml`, `level.yaml`, or `overlay.yaml` contains unknown YAML keys, the system SHALL record each unknown key as a diagnostic note without failing validation.
statements.R2.AC4: WHEN `internal/schema` parses `level.yaml` or `overlay.yaml`, the system SHALL validate required metadata (`schema`, `id`) and optional governance sections (`owners`, `approvers`, `charter`, `constraints`, `exceptions`, and overlay `strength`/`activation`).
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN `internal/schema` parses a valid rule Markdown file, the system SHALL extract frontmatter fields (`id` matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)+$`, `title`, `severity` in `MUST|SHOULD|MAY`, `enforcement` defaulting to `prompt`, `scope` defaulting to `["**/*"]`, `overrides`, `overridable`, `checker`, `guard`, `tags`, `version`, `status` defaulting to `active`) and Markdown body sections (statement paragraph, `Why`, `Rationalizations`, and `Examples` with `Compliant`/`Non-compliant`).
statements.R3.AC2: IF a rule file is missing YAML frontmatter, misses `id`/`title`/`severity`/statement, uses an invalid `id`/`severity`/`enforcement`, or declares `enforcement: check` without `checker` or `enforcement: hook` without `guard`, THEN the system SHALL reject the file with a validation error.
statements.R3.AC3: The system SHALL derive a rule's effective `level` exclusively from its containing level container rather than its `id` prefix or frontmatter.
statements.R3.AC4: WHEN a rule frontmatter contains unknown YAML keys, the system SHALL record each unknown key as a diagnostic note without failing validation.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl init` runs in a directory without `gradus.yaml`, the system SHALL create `gradus.yaml` (`schema: gradus/v1`), `.gradus/levels/project/level.yaml`, an example rule in `.gradus/levels/project/rules/`, and append missing Gradus git-ignore patterns (`.gradus/cache/`, `.gradus/evidence/`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.agents/rules/gradus-user-*.md`) to `.gitignore` while preserving existing `.gitignore` lines.
statements.R4.AC2: IF `gradus.yaml` already exists and `--force` is not specified, THEN `gradusctl init` SHALL leave existing files untouched and exit with code `2`.
statements.R4.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl init --json` succeeds, the system SHALL write a valid JSON summary containing the created and updated file paths to stdout and exit with code `0`.
statements.R5.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl explain <id>` is run for a rule present in local configured levels, the system SHALL print the rule ID, title, derived level, source, severity, enforcement, scope, statement, rationale, rejected rationalizations, examples, and `overrides` target if set, and exit with code `0`.
statements.R5.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl explain <id> --json` is run for an existing rule, the system SHALL emit structured JSON containing the rule metadata, derived level, source provenance, body fields, and any diagnostic notes, and exit with code `0`.
statements.R5.AC3: IF `<id>` is not found in any configured local level OR the repository configuration is missing/invalid, THEN `gradusctl explain <id>` SHALL print a diagnostic error to stderr and exit with code `2`.

statements.C1: Must align strictly with the existing CLI surface implemented in F1–F6 (`gradusctl init`, `resolve`, `compile`, `verify`, `check`, `evidence`, `conflicts`, `lessons`, `reconcile`).
statements.NFR1: **Zero External Runtime Dependencies:** All six skills remain embedded in the static `gradusctl` binary via `skills/embed.go` (`//go:embed gradus-*/*.md`).
statements.NFR2: **Canonical English & Conciseness:** All skill prompts and eval scenarios are written in canonical English and avoid bloated boilerplate so agent context budgets stay lean.
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl compile` targets `claude-code` or `antigravity`, the embedded `skills.FS` SHALL provide `gradus-onboard/SKILL.md`, `gradus-author/SKILL.md`, `gradus-review/SKILL.md`, `gradus-learn/SKILL.md`, `gradus-reconcile/SKILL.md`, and `gradus-conflicts/SKILL.md` without `gradus-placeholder`.
statements.R1.AC2: WHEN any canonical skill `SKILL.md` is parsed, the skill file SHALL include valid YAML frontmatter (`name` matching its directory name and non-empty `description`), explicit inputs, outputs, step-by-step `gradusctl` CLI workflow, and explicit prohibitions matching `gradus-design.md` §16.
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN `gradus-onboard` or `gradus-learn` processes repository history or session signals, the skill instructions SHALL forbid applying configuration changes without explicit user approval, forbid sending data outside the active model, and require secret/PII redaction (`gradusctl lessons add`).
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN `gradus-author` or `gradus-reconcile` proposes rule placements or drift resolution, the skill instructions SHALL forbid direct edits to `locked: true` levels and delegate mutations to `gradusctl reconcile` / `gradusctl resolve`.
statements.R2.AC3: WHEN `gradus-review` or `gradus-conflicts` evaluates code or candidate rule pairs, the skill instructions SHALL require citing rule ID, level, severity, provenance, and confidence, forbidding low-confidence violations, and recording evidence/findings strictly through `gradusctl` (`evidence` / `conflicts`).
statements.R3.AC1: The repository SHALL include at least one scenario specification under `evals/skills/` for each of the six MVP skills (plus a prompt-injection resistance scenario per §22), recording baseline failures/rationalizations and expected skill-guided behavior.
statements.R3.AC2: WHEN `go test ./skills/...` runs, the test suite SHALL deterministically verify `skills.FS` embedding, frontmatter validity, absence of `gradus-placeholder`, and full mapping between the six skills and `evals/skills/` scenarios.

statements.C1: Builds on `internal/schema` from F1 (`core-schema-init`) and adds `github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4` for scope glob comparison/matching.
statements.C2: Implements ADR 0001 (CI override restriction) and ADR 0004 (container-derived level).
statements.NFR1: **Performance:** `gradusctl status --brief` MUST complete in under 100ms on local cached pyramids with zero network I/O.
statements.NFR2: **Deterministic Subprocess Git (D-69):** Git source fetching MUST invoke the system `git` binary via `os/exec` with no CGO or `go-git` dependencies.
statements.NFR3: **Exit Code Semantics (D-73):** `0` = clean pass, `1` = conflicts/violations, `2` = error (lock tamper, missing ref/unreachable `fail-closed` source, unknown override target, invalid schema).
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN a level or overlay specifies `source.path`, the system SHALL resolve its directory on disk while skipping `~/` home-directory levels when the `CI` environment variable is set.
statements.R1.AC2: WHEN a level or overlay specifies `source.git` and `source.ref`, the system SHALL fetch the specified ref into `.gradus/cache/` using the system `git` binary via `os/exec` and record the resolved commit SHA.
statements.R1.AC3: IF a remote `source.git` is unreachable and `offline.mode` is `cache` with an unexpired cached copy within `max_age`, THEN the system SHALL use the cached copy and emit a diagnostic note.
statements.R1.AC4: IF a remote `source.git` is unreachable and `offline.mode` is `fail-closed` OR the cache is missing/expired, THEN the system SHALL fail resolution and exit with code `2`.
statements.R2.AC1: The system SHALL compute a deterministic SHA-256 hash over a level or overlay directory by sorting normalized slash paths lexicographically and normalizing `\r\n` line endings to `\n`.
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl resolve --write` succeeds, the system SHALL write `gradus.lock` containing `schema: gradus/v1`, `definition_hash`, `entries` for all non-`user` levels and overlays, and `view_hash`.
statements.R2.AC3: IF an existing `gradus.lock` is present and a `locked: true` level or overlay on disk or in cache has a hash differing from its recorded lock entry, THEN the system SHALL reject resolution as a lock integrity error and exit with code `2`.
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN resolving the pyramid, the system SHALL order levels as declared in `gradus.yaml`, insert each active overlay immediately after the level matching its `strength`, drop `retired` rules, exclude `draft` rules by default, and mark rules covered by unexpired exceptions in `.gradus/exceptions/` as waived for their scopes.
statements.R3.AC2: IF a lower-level definition violates inherited `constraints` from an upper level's `level.yaml` (`require_levels`, `max_extra_levels`, `allowed_overlays`), THEN the system SHALL report the constraint violation as a blocking conflict.
statements.R3.AC3: IF a lower-level rule declares `overrides: <ID>` targeting an unknown rule ID OR a committed level targets a `user`-level rule (ADR 0001), THEN the system SHALL fail resolution with exit code `2`.
statements.R3.AC4: IF a rule duplicates an existing rule ID without `overrides`, OR weakens `severity`, widens `scope`, or weakens `enforcement` on a non-overridable rule, OR overrides a rule in a `locked: true` level not listed in `editable_rules`, THEN the system SHALL record a blocking conflict in the resolved view.
statements.R3.AC5: WHEN confirmed semantic conflicts exist in `.gradus/findings/`, the system SHALL include them as blocking entries in `conflicts`.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl resolve` runs on a conflict-free pyramid, the system SHALL emit the resolved view (including `view_hash`, `lock_hash`, `levels`, `overlays`, `rules`, `conflicts`, `exceptions`, and `budget`) as text or `--json` and exit with code `0`.
statements.R4.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl resolve` detects one or more blocking conflicts, the system SHALL still emit the resolved view with `conflicts` populated and exit with code `1`.
statements.R4.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl status` or `gradusctl status --brief` runs in a Gradus repository, the system SHALL report lock state, conflict count, and pending lesson count in text or `--json` without making network calls.

statements.C1: Must use only approved dependencies (`github.com/spf13/cobra`, `github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4`, and Go standard library) and build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
statements.C2: Must reuse `internal/resolve` (with `IncludeUser: true` and `OfflineOnly: true`) and `internal/schema` rather than duplicating pyramid or rule parsing logic.
statements.C3: Must preserve ADR 0003: `.agents/hooks.json` and `.claude/settings.json` remain static dispatchers invoking `gradusctl guard`.
statements.NFR1: **Latency Budget:** Evaluating a typical local pyramid with `gradusctl guard` must complete in `< 100ms` (excluding cold OS process startup in CI containers) with zero network I/O.
statements.NFR2: **Cross-Platform Path Safety:** Protected governance path matching must normalize Windows backslashes (`\`) and absolute paths rooted inside the workspace into clean relative slash paths so anti-tamper cannot be bypassed via `.\gradus.yaml`, `./gradus.yaml`, or absolute workspace paths.
statements.NFR3: **Fail-Closed Technical Safety:** Configuration errors, lock tampering, or malformed hook payloads must return exit code `2` and never silently pass as `allow`.
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl guard` receives a valid Claude Code `PreToolUse` JSON payload on `stdin` (such as `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, or `MultiEdit` with `tool_input`), the system SHALL normalize the invocation into a canonical action class (`command` or `write`) and target string (shell command or normalized slash-separated path).
statements.R1.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl guard` receives a valid Antigravity `PreToolUse` JSON payload on `stdin` (such as `run_command`, `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`, or `multi_replace_file_content` with `tool_input`), the system SHALL normalize the invocation into the same canonical action class (`command` or `write`) and target string.
statements.R1.AC3: WHEN `stdin` is empty, malformed JSON, or missing required tool identification, the system SHALL fail closed with exit code `2` and an actionable diagnostic error rather than returning `allow`.
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN a file-writing or file-editing tool targets any protected governance path (`gradus.yaml`, `gradus.lock`, `.gradus/**`, `.walden/**`, `.agents/hooks.json`, or `.claude/settings.json`), the system SHALL require at least `ask` (explicit human confirmation) even when no explicit user or project hook rule matches the path.
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN both built-in anti-tamper (`ask`) and an explicit `enforcement: hook` rule with `decision: deny` match the same governance target, the system SHALL resolve the decision to `deny`.
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN evaluating a normalized tool invocation against the local resolved view, the system SHALL load the repository pyramid together with `~/.gradus/levels/user` (when present) using local files/cache only and zero network calls.
statements.R3.AC2: WHEN evaluating active, non-waived `enforcement: hook` rules, the system SHALL match `guard.action` (`command`/`bash` against shell commands, `write`/`edit` against file paths), `guard.pattern` (regular expression for commands; doublestar glob or regex for paths), and rule `scope` (when a target file path is known).
statements.R3.AC3: WHEN multiple hook rules or built-in anti-tamper match the same invocation, the system SHALL combine decisions using strict precedence `deny > ask > allow` and report all matched rule IDs and reasons.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl guard` completes evaluation, the system SHALL output a JSON payload containing `decision` (`allow` | `ask` | `deny`), `reason`, `matched_rules`, `anti_tamper`, and a `hookSpecificOutput` block (`hookEventName: "PreToolUse"`, `permissionDecision`, `permissionDecisionReason`).
statements.R4.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl guard` exits, the system SHALL return exit code `0` for `allow` or `ask`, exit code `1` for `deny`, and exit code `2` for technical errors (malformed payload, invalid regex pattern, unreadable/invalid configuration, or lock tamper).

statements.NFR1: **No Error-as-Pass Guarantee (D-73):** Missing checkers, broken git diff commands, or invalid lockfiles MUST return exit code `2`, never `0`.
statements.NFR2: **Subprocess Safety (`os/exec`):** All `git diff`, external checker, and `command` sink invocations MUST use `os/exec` with zero shell interpolation unless explicitly configured in `command` sink.
statements.NFR3: **Zero Personal Metrics (P16):** Evidence records MUST contain no user-activity tracking beyond standard git commit metadata.
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl verify` runs on a valid, conflict-free pyramid whose `gradus.lock` matches locked levels and whose compiled target files match `PlanCompile` byte-for-byte, the system SHALL exit with code `0`.
statements.R1.AC2: IF the pyramid has blocking conflicts, expired exceptions, OR any compiled target file on disk differs from `PlanCompile` (drift), THEN `gradusctl verify` SHALL report each finding with file/rule context and exit with code `1`.
statements.R1.AC3: IF `gradus.yaml` is invalid, `gradus.lock` is missing or mismatches a `locked: true` level, OR a `fail-closed` source is unreachable, THEN `gradusctl verify` SHALL report the error and exit with code `2`.
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl check` runs with `--staged` or `--base <ref>`, the system SHALL determine changed files in scope using `git diff` via `os/exec` and filter rules with `enforcement: check` whose `scope` globs match the changed files (skipping waived rules).
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN a matching `check` rule uses the built-in pattern checker (`checker.name: pattern` or `regex`), the system SHALL scan the changed files and report any match with rule ID, severity, level, source, file path, and line number, exiting with code `1`.
statements.R2.AC3: WHEN a matching `check` rule specifies an external checker (`checker.name` such as `gitleaks`, `semgrep`, or a custom binary), the system SHALL invoke the external checker on the scoped files and map non-zero violation exits to `1`.
statements.R2.AC4: IF a configured external checker binary is missing from `PATH` OR exits with an execution/configuration error, THEN `gradusctl check` SHALL fail with exit code `2` and NEVER report a pass.
statements.R3.AC1: The system SHALL produce evidence records conforming to `spec/v1/schema/evidence.schema.json` (`schema: gradus/v1`, `id`, `kind`, `timestamp`, `commit`, `lock_hash`, `view_hash`, `producer`, `findings`, `verdict`) with zero personal activity metrics (P16).
statements.R3.AC2: WHEN writing evidence, the system SHALL support all 5 sink types (`none`, `local` in `.gradus/evidence/`, `ci-artifact` directory, `repo` committed path, and `command` piped via stdin), selecting `evidence.ci.sinks` when `CI` is set if configured.
statements.R3.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl evidence list` or `gradusctl evidence write` runs, the system SHALL list local `.gradus/evidence/*.json` records (pruning expired records past retention) or write an evidence record to configured sinks.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl hooks` runs with `hooks.manager: auto`, the system SHALL detect `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (`pre-commit`), `lefthook.yml` (`lefthook`), `.husky/` (`husky`), or fall back to `native` (`.githooks/`) in that order.
statements.R4.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl hooks print` or `gradusctl hooks install` runs, the system SHALL emit the manager-specific configuration snippet running `gradusctl verify` and `gradusctl check --staged`, and with `install` write/update the hook config (requiring explicit `--native` consent before modifying `core.hooksPath`).
